rationale: A smaller 20x21 boolean canvas was expanded with two all-false tensors. A single Pad encodes the same bottom/right extension with a tiny pads vector and one scalar false value.
A 20x20 uint8 canvas used nested zero concatenation for the right and bottom margins. Input-style Pad keeps the spatial contract while removing the serialized zero margins.
The final channel stack is logically boolean. Keeping the tail boolean until the output boundary avoids larger numeric intermediates.
Boolean channel concatenation is cheaper than carrying numeric one-hot planes through the final tail.
For small graphs, a few tail tensors dominate cost; removing the numeric tail gives a large relative gain.
An equality-style one-hot tail can be represented with boolean masks before the final output conversion.
The one-hot construction is cheaper when the logical mask stays in a compact type.
The selected artifact preserves validation behavior with fewer profiled memory-plus-parameter units.
A cost-aware artifact choice gives a small but stable task-level reduction.
